hero.headline: Key Biscayne Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Treat Key Biscayne accurately as an incorporated village between two major parks on a barrier island south of Miami Beach.

overview: Treat Key Biscayne accurately as an incorporated village between two major parks on a barrier island south of Miami Beach.
The best guide distinguishes the village itself from county-managed Crandon Park to the north and Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park to the south.

thingsToDo.title: Village of Key Biscayne
thingsToDo.description: Use the compact village for restaurants, local services, and access to the island's central beaches.

thingsToDo.title: Crandon Park — county park
thingsToDo.description: North of the village, this Miami-Dade County park offers beach, picnic, and nature areas and should not be labeled a village park.

thingsToDo.title: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
thingsToDo.description: South of the village, the Florida state park protects beaches, coastal habitat, and Cape Florida Lighthouse.

thingsToDo.title: Cape Florida Lighthouse
thingsToDo.description: Visit the historic lighthouse within Bill Baggs for one of the island's clearest landmarks and broad coastal views when access is available.

thingsToDo.title: Biscayne Bay paddling
thingsToDo.description: Use calm-water paddling or boating to understand the island's relationship to the bay, mangroves, and mainland skyline.

thingsToDo.title: Rickenbacker Causeway and Virginia Key
thingsToDo.description: Treat the causeway corridor and Virginia Key as separate geographic areas connecting Key Biscayne to Miami.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Key Biscayne?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is Key Biscayne good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Key Biscayne is an incorporated village on a barrier island in Miami-Dade County.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The village occupies the central portion of the island, with Crandon Park north and Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park south.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: The island's history combines Indigenous use, lighthouse and maritime history, mid-20th-century development, and modern coastal recreation.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Beach time, cycling, paddling, fishing, and park visits are the natural outdoor focus.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: A bike works well on the island, but a car or rideshare is useful for crossing the causeway and connecting to Miami.
